name: Maine
overview: Maine issues air emission licenses. Minor sources and new source review (new equipment or modifications) are licensed under Chapter 115; major sources also need a Part 70 (Title V) license under Chapter 140. All of Maine is in the Ozone Transport Region, so the VOC major source threshold is 50 tons per year. New sources and minor and major modifications require a BACT analysis. General permits cover rock crushers and concrete batch plants.

permitTypes.name: General Permits
permitTypes.description: Rock Crusher General Permit and Concrete Batch Plant General Permit.

permitTypes.name: Chapter 115 Minor Source Air Emission License
permitTypes.description: License for minor sources and for new equipment or modifications (new source review). BACT analysis required for new sources and minor and major modifications. Synthetic minor status is available by taking federally enforceable limits or caps.
permitTypes.thresholds: Per DEP: minor sources have potential to emit below 50 tpy VOC (Ozone Transport Region), 10 tpy any single HAP, 25 tpy combined HAPs, and 100 tpy of any other regulated pollutant.

permitTypes.name: Chapter 115 Major New Source / Major Modification
permitTypes.description: Major new sources and major modifications are licensed under Chapter 115 with additional public notice (Notice of Draft License Availability) and major source application guidance.

permitTypes.name: Part 70 (Title V) Air Emission License
permitTypes.description: Required for major sources in addition to Chapter 115 licensing; separate forms for initial/renewal, modifications, and transfers.
permitTypes.thresholds: Per DEP: 50 tpy VOC (Ozone Transport Region); 10 tpy single HAP; 25 tpy combined HAPs; 100 tpy any other regulated pollutant.

oilAndGas.summary: Maine has no oil and gas production. DEP's permitting pages list no oil-and-gas-specific air program.
